title: rewardRate = rewardBudget / windowDuration floors to zero when budget < windowDuration, stranding dust funds
regression-risk: pre-existing (CS-02 prior audit; rejected as Medium but the underlying dust-stranding remains)
description:
Every rate-computation site uses floor division: `rewardRate = rewardBudget / windowDuration`. When `rewardBudget < windowDuration` (in seconds), the result truncates to zero and `_updatePool` accrues no rewards per second. Across repeated resets each reset also truncates any sub-windowDuration residue — compounding a small amount of dust into stranded funds over the life of the pool.

With `MAX_WINDOW = 10 * 365 days = 315,360,000 seconds`, any residue below ~3.15e8 wei phUSD stays stranded per reset. The absolute per-reset loss is small (~3.15e-10 phUSD), but because resets happen on every user interaction (through `_syncBudget`), the total stranded amount grows with pool lifetime and activity.

This also creates the zero-rate edge case in `ownerOrNotGriefed` (see CS-10 of this report) where the modifier becomes vacuous.
impact: Small, bounded per-reset dust stranding. Accumulates over pool lifetime but remains sub-nanocent per reset. Also interacts with CS-10 to create a modifier-bypass scenario under zero-rate conditions. Not a material value-leak finding on its own, but the compounding with the unconditional reset design makes it worse than a typical 1-wei rounding.
proof:
rewardBudget = 1e8 wei phUSD, windowDuration = 540 days = 46,656,000 sec. rewardRate = 1e8 / 46,656,000 = 2 wei/sec. elapsed = 1 sec. reward = 2. accRewardPerShare += 2 * 1e18 / totalStaked. After 46,656,000 seconds (540 days), total reward = 2 * 46,656,000 = 93,312,000 wei — NOT the full 1e8. 6,688,000 wei is stranded.

Smaller case: rewardBudget = 1e7 wei (below windowDuration). rewardRate = 0. No emissions. All 1e7 wei stranded until a top-up raises the budget above 46,656,000 wei.
suggested-fix: Use higher-precision rate: `rewardRate = (rewardBudget * ACC_PRECISION) / windowDuration`, and in `_updatePool` compute `reward = (elapsed * rewardRate) / ACC_PRECISION`. This shifts the truncation down by 18 decimals. Alternatively, track accrual as `rewardBudget * elapsed / windowDuration` directly and avoid the intermediate `rewardRate` variable. Either approach eliminates the dust-stranding and the zero-rate edge case simultaneously.
